subject: ss-infectious-diseases
title: Glycopeptides, daptomycin, linezolid and other antibacterials: high-yield essentials

steps.tx: Enterococci cause serious bloodstream and endocardial infections, and **E. faecium** carries the worst prognosis because it is often resistant to ampicillin and vancomycin. Start by identifying the species and testing ampicillin, vancomycin and high-level aminoglycoside resistance. Confirm vancomycin resistance by detecting **vanA or vanB** genes.

rows: Ampicillin plus ceftriaxone, or a penicillin with an aminoglycoside
Linezolid, tedizolid or daptomycin per susceptibility

steps.tx: **Daptomycin** is a lipopeptide that depolarises the bacterial cell membrane, causing rapid cell death against susceptible gram-positive organisms. It is inactivated by pulmonary surfactant, so it must never be used for pneumonia. Renal impairment prolongs its half-life, and dosing interval is extended to every 48 hours when creatinine clearance falls below 30 mL/min.

right.title: Daptomycin cautions
points: Monitor CPK weekly beyond one week

steps.tx: Daptomycin myopathy is the key toxicity. If CPK rises above five times the upper limit of normal with symptoms, **stop daptomycin**. Check CPK weekly for courses longer than one week, and pause the statin during therapy. Use an elastomeric pump with caution, since it can leach **2-mercaptobenzothiazole** into the drug solution. Do not shake the vial vigorously.

steps.tx: **Linezolid** is an oxazolidinone that blocks 70S initiation by binding the 23S rRNA of the 50S subunit, so it is bacteriostatic. It is a nonselective MAO inhibitor, so avoid serotonergic drugs and pseudoephedrine. Watch for myelosuppression, so check a weekly complete blood count, and for optic or peripheral neuropathy after 28 days. Oral bioavailability is near 100 percent.

rows: Avoid SSRIs; treat with benzodiazepines, cooling, cyproheptadine
Weekly CBC; filgrastim helps severe neutropenia
Risk rises beyond 28 days of therapy

steps.tx: **Vancomycin** inhibits peptidoglycan polymerisation by binding D-alanyl-D-alanine. Systemic doses should run over at least 60 minutes; if flushing occurs, slow the infusion rather than stopping. Oral vancomycin is poorly absorbed and is used for **Clostridioides difficile** colitis, and needs no renal adjustment. In fluid-restricted patients, concentrations up to 10 mg/mL are acceptable.
